claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are crystalline, compositionally homogeneous, and fully solid.
Thermally induced Cu surface segregation governs the onset and progression of phase transitions in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu is the low-melting-point constituent of the FeNiCrCoCu system.
Cu enrichment at the nanoparticle surface facilitates formation of a liquid-like surface layer.
The liquid-like surface layer propagates from the surface into the nanoparticle interior.
A surface coating or adsorbed inert ligand can hinder Cu surface segregation.
Cu surface enrichment produces a thin liquid-like layer below the bulk melting point.
During heating, Cu atoms preferentially segregate to the nanoparticle surface because of their lower cohesive energy.
Cu segregation locally lowers the barrier to melting.
The premelted surface layer accelerates melting of the underlying lattice through enhanced diffusion and reduced bonding constraints.
Untreated nanoparticles will begin surface premelting earlier than nanoparticles whose surfaces are modified to suppress Cu segregation.
Untreated nanoparticles will have a lower effective melting point than surface-modified nanoparticles.
Melting will progress through a surface-initiated cascade.
Oxidation, extremely rapid heating, or surface-active contaminants may alter the proposed behavior.
Surface segregation is well documented in bimetallic nanoparticle systems.
Direct evidence for segregation-controlled melting in complex high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is limited.
